titleStmt.title: Suggested Letter to the President of Panama

div.head: Suggested Letter to the President of Panama
div.p: I stated in my letter of April sixth, 1959 that I would direct a study to be made by competent experts in my Government of the points raised in the Memorandum accompanying your letter of March seventh, 1959.
The results of this study are contained in an Aide Memoire which is being delivered through the usual diplomatic channels.

May I take this opportunity to reiterate the hope expressed in my letter of July twenty-fifth, 1958, that adoption of these new employment and wage practices will make a significant contribution to the mutual respect and friendship existing between our Governments and peoples. I firmly believe that any differences existing with regard to the implementation of the new system can be resolved by patient discussion and negotiation between your Government and the officials of the United States charged with the responsibility of administering it.
Please accept, Mr. President, my personal good wishes to you and to the people of Panama.

note.p: In telegram 21 to Panama City, July 13, the Department of State informed Ambassador Harrington that he was to deliver the text of this letter from President Eisenhower to Panamanian Foreign Minister Moreno as soon as possible, and that he was to inform the Foreign Minister that the Embassy also had received instructions to resubmit the text of the Aide Mémoire of June 24. (611.1913/7–959) In telegram 30 from Panama City, July 15, Harrington notified the Department that he had delivered the text of the President’s letter to Moreno and had notified the Foreign Minister of his intention to resubmit the Aide Mémoire of June 24. (611.1913/7–1559) In telegram 39 from Panama City, July 17, Harrington reported that Moreno had urged the Embassy to make certain textual changes in the Aide Mémoire before its presentation to the Government of Panama. Harrington endorsed Moreno’s suggestions as a way to end the controversy surrounding the Aide Mémoire. (711.11–EI/7–1759) In telegram 30 to Panama City, July 17, the Department accepted Harrington’s recommendations concerning the Aide Mémoire. (711.11–EI/7–1759) In telegram 43 from Panama City, July 20, Harrington notified the Department that Moreno had accepted the revised Aide Mémoire. (711.11–EI/7–2059) The Embassy at Panama City transmitted the text of the Aide Mémoire to the Department for its information under cover of desp. 44, July 20, not printed. (611.1913/7–2059)
